$comment: Raised 292 -> 297 for myne-md/myne#529. `e2e/agent-run.e2e.ts` is NEW
relative to develop and carries FIVE scenarios (ag1 through ag5), all
inside `aiDescribe` and all executing where CI sets MYNE_E2E_AI=1.
An earlier version of this file said +2 and gave the reason as the file
'gaining ag4 and ag5'. That was true against an intermediate state of the
branch and false against develop, which is the only baseline this number
means anything relative to. A floor understated by three would have let
ag1, ag2 and ag3 stop executing with the gate still green, which is the
exact failure the floor exists to catch.
This is arithmetic on a CI-measured base, not a new measurement. The 292
came from CI (pipeline 431); CI already runs this file, since its e2e step
sets MYNE_E2E_AI=1 and builds with `local-inference-stub`. Locally all five
pass three times consecutively in the container
(scripts/e2e-ai-buildrun.sh).
`stable_max_failures` 33 -> 0, and this one IS a fresh measurement. CI
pipeline 643 ran the stable lane at 311 passed and 0 failed, and the whole
suite passes locally in one warm container too. The 33 dated from pipeline
431 and had stopped describing anything: a ceiling eleven times the actual
count permits a regression to land silently, which is the one thing a
ratchet exists to prevent. The earlier note here said not to guess the new
number from a laptop and to let CI measure it; CI has now measured it.
Zero is a real gate rather than a slack one, and that is deliberate: the
standing failures it used to absorb were not flake, they were seven
distinct permanent-state bugs (myne-md/myne#529, and `e2e/CLAUDE.md`
records the class). If a future run goes red here, the honest move is to
diagnose it, not to raise this number back up. Raising a ceiling to make a
red pipeline green is the one edit that is never legitimate.
The FLOOR stays at 297 rather than rising to the 311 that ran. A floor is a
claim about how many scenarios must EXECUTE, and legitimate skips exist
(the sync specs self-skip without a myne-server binary, and the AI family
skips without MYNE_E2E_AI). Pinning it to one run's exact count would fail
on the next legitimate skip while catching nothing the current number
misses.
297 -> 298 for myne-md/myne#533, which adds ag6 to `e2e/agent-run.e2e.ts`.
ag6 drives the ONE composer through both of its modes into one transcript:
the whole of what that issue changed, and the only scenario that would
catch a regression re-adding the second composer, since every other one
drives whichever input its own testid happens to find.
Same arithmetic as the +5 above and on the same CI-measured base: ag6 sits
inside `aiDescribe`, and CI's e2e step sets MYNE_E2E_AI=1 and builds with
`local-inference-stub` (.woodpecker/e2e.yml), so it executes there.
MEASURED, not reasoned. `scripts/e2e-ai-buildrun.sh agent-run agent-run
agent-run` ran green three consecutive times in one warm container on
2026-08-20, 6 of 6 scenarios passing each time with none skipped, which is
`e2e/CLAUDE.md`'s definition of done for a new scenario. That run also
covers ag1 to ag5, which this branch retargeted onto the new
`ai.composer-*` testids, so the +1 is the only count that moved but six
scenarios were re-proven.
Raised 298 -> 301 for myne-md/myne#534. Three NEW scenarios relative to
develop: gt2 and gt3 in `e2e/graph-tab.e2e.ts` (the graph body fills the
pane; the canvas follows a pane resize) and tp4 in `e2e/task-panel.e2e.ts`
(the task body fills the pane). None carries a self-skip beyond the platform
gate every scenario has, so all three execute wherever the suite does.
The BASE moved while this branch was in review, and the +3 is what carries
over rather than the total. It was written as 297 -> 300 against the base
myne-md/myne#533 has since raised to 298, and taking either side of that
merge whole would have silently dropped one branch's scenarios from the
floor: 300 loses ag6, 298 loses all three of these. Adding the deltas is the
only resolution that keeps both claims, which is the failure this file
exists to catch, one merge earlier than it usually catches it.
Arithmetic on a CI-measured base, not a new measurement, which is the same
basis both entries above used. Locally all three pass three times
consecutively in one warm container, and all three were also run against a
build with the production fix REVERTED, where each failed on its own
assertion rather than on a timeout: 347 px for gt2, a 260 px stale backing
store for gt3, 568 px for tp4.
Leaving the floor flat is the failure this file exists to catch, and its own
#529 note spells it out: three scenarios could later stop executing with
`e2e-floor` still green. `stable_max_failures` stays 0.
Raised 301 -> 302 for myne-md/myne#520. One NEW scenario relative to develop:
nco3 in `e2e/note-cover.e2e.ts`, which builds a split, focuses the left pane
and presses Remove on the RIGHT pane's banner. It carries no self-skip beyond
the platform gate every scenario has, so it executes wherever the suite does.
Same arithmetic on the same CI-measured base as the entries above. MEASURED:
`scripts/e2e-buildrun.sh note-cover note-cover note-cover` ran green three
consecutive times in one warm container on 2026-08-22, 3 of 3 scenarios each
time with none skipped. It was also run against a build with the production
fix REVERTED (`src/editor-host.ts` back to a detail-free
`new CustomEvent(REMOVE_COVER_EVENT)`), where it failed on its own assertion,
naming the left pane as the note that lost its cover, rather than on a
timeout.
That revert run is worth more than usual here. An earlier attempt reported the
same failure against a build that HAD the fix, because the frontend is
embedded at compile time and a frontend-only change relinks nothing: the
binary in the shared `myne-e2e-target` volume was still serving another
worktree's bundle. `scripts/e2e-buildrun.sh` now touches the crate root, and
`e2e/CLAUDE.md` records the trap. Until that was found, a green build was
producing the worst possible wrong answer, that a correct fix does not work.
`stable_max_failures` stays 0.
Floor STAYS 302 through myne-md/myne#522's E2E work, and that is the correct
arithmetic rather than an omission. `cb1` in `e2e/clipboard-copy.e2e.ts` gained
the Save-as-file arm (the page-seat `plugin:dialog|save` interception that
`note-export.e2e.ts` ne3 templates, then an equality assertion on the SAVE
sentence and a 24-word length check on the file that actually landed). That is
assertions inside an existing `it`, not a new scenario, so the count the floor
measures does not move.
MEASURED both ways. `scripts/e2e-buildrun.sh clipboard-copy` passes 2 of 2, and
against a build with `announce(feedback.onSuccess)` deleted from the dialog arm
of `saveSecretAsTextFile` it fails on its own assertion, naming the save
sentence, rather than on a timeout somewhere else.
Floor 302 -> 303 for `trs1` in `e2e/task-row-selection.e2e.ts`, added in
myne-md/myne#520's review. One scenario, one `it`.
It covers the step the unit lanes structurally cannot reach, and there are two
of those. `tests/editor/taskRowSelection.test.ts` asserts the DECISION,
`trimRowNewline` as a pure function with every refusal branch and the
reverse-drag direction. `tests/editor/taskLineEditing.test.ts` asserts the
WIRING: a mounted CM6 view, a dispatched `select.pointer` transaction, the
resulting selection and DOM. Neither produces that transaction from a GESTURE,
because CM6 runs its triple-click handler off `event.detail` and jsdom has no
detail-aware selection model. The bug lived in that step, and its symptom is a
caret one visual ROW below the row the user clicked, which is a rendered-DOM
fact this is the only lane with a layout for.
MEASURED both ways. `scripts/e2e-buildrun.sh task-row-selection` passes 1 of 1,
and against a build with `taskRowSelection()` removed from the extension array
it fails on its own assertion, naming the row the focus end landed on, rather
than on a timeout somewhere else.
What this scenario does NOT cover, stated rather than left absent: the four
`Cmd-ArrowLeft` / `Cmd-ArrowRight` / `Cmd-Backspace` / `Cmd-Delete` chords in
`editor/src/line-boundary.ts` are declared `mac:`-only, matching the
`defaultKeymap` bindings they shadow. This lane is a Linux container, so those
bindings are not installed in it at all and no scenario here can press them.
Their probe-versus-fallback branch depends on real `coordsAtPos` geometry, so
jsdom cannot cover it either and the unit tests stub the probe. That leaves
them covered by unit tests over stubbed geometry plus the manual pass, and the
gap is named here rather than discovered later: closing it needs a macOS E2E
seat, which this project does not have.
Floor RAISED 303 -> 308 for myne-md/myne#482 and #483.
`e2e/screen-capture-override.e2e.ts` is NEW and carries five scenarios: the
escape reachable by Tab while clipped and writing nothing until confirmed
(sc1), the override surviving a restart (sc2), the process flag reported
apart from the file (sc3), a flag-launched run honouring what the file
already said (sc4), and the escape one Shift+Tab from the autofocused
password field on Unlock (sc5).
Raised only AFTER observing them run, which is the rule this file's own
history keeps re-learning: `./scripts/e2e-buildrun.sh` with the spec passed
three times plus `acl-refusal`, one build and four runs in the same warm
container, 5 passed each time and 0 failed. A floor raised for scenarios
nobody has seen execute is a floor that certifies nothing.
`acl-refusal` ran in that batch deliberately rather than incidentally. This
change removes `core:window:allow-show` from `capabilities/default.json`
(its one consumer, the reveal after idle auto-lock, now asks the host for a
fixed protect/show/protect/focus sequence instead of driving the window
itself), and `plugin:window|show` was `acl1`'s POSITIVE control. Left alone,
the repo's only scenario that observes Tauri ENFORCING the ACL would have
gone red on its control rather than on its subject, which is worse than a
missing test. The control is `plugin:window|is_visible` now, a read inside
`core:window:default`, and the batch above is the evidence that it answers.
`stable_max_failures` stays 0.
